bull.b: Low leverage and a relatively large equity base provide durable financial flexibility, lowering insolvency risk and giving management runway to fund regulatory milestones, commercialization set-up, and R&D without immediate forced debt refinancing. This supports strategic optionality over months.

Two successful pivotal trials materially reduce clinical and regulatory risk for elegrobart, supporting a planned BLA and potential approvals. This structural achievement raises the probability of future revenues and gives the company a sustainable competitive position in thyroid eye disease.

A multi-year agreement with WuXi secures scalable, quality-controlled supply for veligrotug, reducing operational and launch execution risk. Non-exclusive terms and rolling forecasts add flexibility, helping ensure product availability and predictable COGS as commercial volumes scale.

bear.b: Sustained negative operating and free cash flow creates a structural financing need until product sales ramp. Persistent burn pressures liquidity, forces reliance on capital markets or partnerships, and constrains the firm's ability to invest in broader programs without dilution over the coming months.

Very large net losses and negative margins reflect a high fixed-cost R&D and SG&A base relative to current revenue. These structural losses will challenge cash runway and operational scalability until commercial revenues materialize and cost absorption improves at scale.

Recent sizable equity and convertible debt raises improve runway but create dilution and conversion risk. Dependence on capital markets is a structural vulnerability: repeated raises or conversion could dilute shareholders and influence strategy until sustainable product cash flows replace funding reliance.
